claims.text: Formation and crystal-structure selection under rapid thermal processing is governed by a critical maximum-processing-temperature threshold.
Above the critical temperature, atomic diffusion rates overcome surface-energy-driven nucleation barriers.
Above the critical temperature, homogeneous FCC solid-solution nuclei grow beyond the critical nucleus size and produce single-phase nanoparticles.
Below the critical temperature, insufficient diffusion causes phase separation.
Below the critical temperature, insufficient diffusion causes elemental segregation.
Below the critical temperature, insufficient diffusion produces irregular particle morphology.
Rapid heating and cooling at approximately 1000 °C yields an equimolar Ir-Pt-Pd-Au-Rh single-phase FCC solid solution.
The initial single-phase nanoparticles have a diameter of approximately 5 nm.
Sharp FCC XRD peaks and uniform TEM-EDS elemental maps confirm the stated initial single-phase FCC state.
Element-specific surface energies set the nucleation barrier and contribute to determining critical nucleus size.
Temperature-dependent atomic diffusivities contribute to determining critical nucleus size.
The critical maximum processing temperature is approximately 800 °C for equimolar Ir-Pt-Pd-Au-Rh under the specified rapid thermal conditions.
At or above the threshold temperature, XRD will show single-phase FCC peaks with narrow FWHM.
At or above the threshold temperature, TEM-EDS maps will show uniform elemental distributions.
Below the threshold temperature, XRD will show multiple or broadened peaks.
Below the threshold temperature, elemental segregation will occupy at least 20% of particle volume.
Below the threshold temperature, particles will exhibit irregular shapes.
The proposed threshold may vary by approximately ±50 °C because multicomponent diffusion coefficients are uncertain.
Surface energies in the five-element Ir-Pt-Pd-Au-Rh system are not precisely known.

contradictions.description: The query requires nanoparticles containing more than five elements, whereas the proposed system is exactly five elements: Ir, Pt, Pd, Au, and Rh.
